synopsis: A rehearsal sentence stops at one blank author name even though the atlas passed through many hands. From the chair by the window, Peter asks whether the sentence is wrong rather than any of the names. The learner identifies the counterfactual response that tests that premise; Sophie rewrites the spoken introduction around traceable contributions, and the class tries it from the stage before turning to the next blank cue: what each person will do after the final night.

forbiddenClaims: surname, guessed kana name, nationality, job, or private history

scenes.goal: Stop a first-page rehearsal at the sentence demanding one maker, and reach the point where the sentence itself becomes the thing to revise.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: When the spoken introduction leaves room for one name, does the class pick someone or question the line?
scenes.learnerNeed: A recognition check where the learner identifies the frame-shifting counterfactual that challenges the single-owner premise without blaming anyone in the room.

nodes.description: The projector holds on the rehearsal line 「このアトラスを作ったのは、＿＿です」. On the board, Sophie's first attempt at the blank has become a row of crossed-out names. The atlas lies open on the lectern. By the window, the chair no one thought to check is occupied after all; Peter watches with his notebook shut on one knee.

nodes.intent: Stop the rehearsal where its one-name sentence erases a different contributor whichever name she tries.
nodes.attentionTarget: the spoken blank and the crossed-out names beneath it

n3.japanese: また、ここで止まる。『このアトラスを作ったのは、＿＿です』。一人入れると、道を足した人か、文を直した人が消える。空けたままだと読めないし。
n3.reading: また、ここでとまる。『このアトラスをつくったのは、＿＿です』。ひとりいれると、みちをたしたひとか、ぶんをなおしたひとがきえる。あけたままだとよめないし。
n3.english: We stop here again. 'The person who made this atlas was __.' Put one name in, and either the person who added the route or the person who revised the text disappears. Leave it blank, and the line cannot be read.

n2.japanese: また、ここで止まるんです。『このアトラスを作ったのは、＿＿です』。一人入れると、道を足した人か、後で文を直した人が消える。かといって、空欄のまま舞台では読めない。
n2.reading: また、ここでとまるんです。『このアトラスをつくったのは、＿＿です』。ひとりいれると、みちをたしたひとか、あとでぶんをなおしたひとがきえる。かといって、くうらんのままぶたいではよめない。
n2.english: We stop here again. 'The person who made this atlas was __.' Put one name in, and either the person who added the route or the person who later revised the text disappears. But we cannot read a blank aloud on stage.

n1.japanese: また、ここで止まるんです。『このアトラスを作ったのは、＿＿です』。誰か一人を入れると、道を引いた人か、後で文を直した人が消える。だからといって、空欄のまま舞台で読むわけにもいかない。
n1.reading: また、ここでとまるんです。『このアトラスをつくったのは、＿＿です』。だれかひとりをいれると、みちをひいたひとか、あとでぶんをなおしたひとがきえる。だからといって、くうらんのままぶたいでよむわけにもいかない。
n1.english: We stop here again. 'The person who made this atlas was __.' Put one person in, and either the route maker or the later editor disappears. Yet we cannot read a blank aloud on stage.

nodes.intent: From the overlooked seat, question the premise rather than contradict anyone: use a counterfactual and premise-framing to ask whether finishing the atlas ever required a single owner at all.
nodes.attentionTarget: the sentence before the blank, which no one has tried changing

n2.japanese: あの……その文、要りますか。もし名前が一つも残ってなくても、アトラスはここにあるし、みんなで作ってきたことも変わらない。なら、合ってないのは名前じゃなくて、文のほうかも。
n2.reading: あの……そのぶん、いりますか。もしなまえがひとつものこってなくても、アトラスはここにあるし、みんなでつくってきたこともかわらない。なら、あってないのはなまえじゃなくて、ぶんのほうかも。
n2.english: Um… do we need that sentence? Even if no names had survived, the atlas would still be here, and the way everyone made it would not change. Perhaps the sentence is wrong, not the names.

n1.japanese: ……一つだけ。その文、本当に要りますか。仮に、誰一人名前を残していなかったとしても、これはこれで完成していたはずで。だとしたら、合っていないのは名前じゃなくて、文のほうかもしれません。
n1.reading: ……ひとつだけ。そのぶん、ほんとうにいりますか。かりに、だれひとりなまえをのこしていなかったとしても、これはこれでかんせいしていたはずで。だとしたら、あっていないのはなまえじゃなくて、ぶんのほうかもしれません。
n1.english: …One thing. Do we actually need that sentence? Even if nobody had left a name, the atlas would still have been complete. Perhaps the sentence is wrong, not the names.

nodes.intent: Catch the frame-shift and move from 'we have to name one' to questioning who decided that in the first place, opening the premise instead of defending it.
nodes.attentionTarget: the demand for one name, now visible as an assumption rather than a rule

n3.japanese: ……あ。名前を探してたけど、直すのは文のほう? 『誰が作った』じゃなくて、『何を、誰から受け取った』なら言える。
n3.reading: ……あ。なまえをさがしてたけど、なおすのはぶんのほう? 『だれがつくった』じゃなくて、『なにを、だれからうけとった』ならいえる。
n3.english: …Oh. I've been looking for a name, but the sentence is what needs changing? We cannot say 'who made it,' but we can say what came from whom.

n2.japanese: ……あ。ずっと名前を探してたけど、直すのは文のほうなんだ。『誰が作った』じゃなくて、『何を、誰から受け取った』なら、今ある資料で言える。

n2.english: …Oh. I've been looking for a name, but the sentence is what needs changing. We cannot say 'who made it,' but the evidence does let us say what came from whom.

n1.japanese: ……あ。名前を探し続けてたけど、直すのは文のほうなんですね。『誰が作った』ではなく、『何を、誰から受け取った』なら、資料の範囲で言える。
n1.reading: ……あ。なまえをさがしつづけてたけど、なおすのはぶんのほうなんですね。『だれがつくった』ではなく、『なにを、だれからうけとった』なら、しりょうのはんいでいえる。
n1.english: …Oh. I've kept looking for a name, but the sentence is what needs changing. We cannot say 'who made it'; we can say what came from whom, within the evidence we have.

nodes.resume: The projected sentence still stops at one blank name. The learner identifies the counterfactual response that challenges the sentence rather than anyone named on the board.

nodes.resumeContext: The rehearsal line says 「このアトラスを作ったのは、＿＿です」 even though routes, captions, and photographs came from different hands. Choose the response that uses a counterfactual and そもそも to question the one-owner sentence without dismissing anyone in the room.

nodes.description: The crossed-out names stay on the board. On the projector, a bracket now begins before 「このアトラスを作ったのは」 and ends after the blank. No name is circled; the sentence itself waits for another pass.

nodes.resume: The selected response puts the premise in question. Peter looks at the bracketed sentence and names what changed.

nodes.intent: Accept that the class has rejected the false premise and name the move precisely: he shifted the question from 'whose name' to 'is one name needed at all,' questioning the frame instead of a person.
nodes.attentionTarget: the shifted question, and the ease it lets back into the room

n3.japanese: そう、それです。名前を消すんじゃなくて、空欄の前から直す。……消しゴム、まだ残ってますね。
n3.reading: そう、それです。なまえをけすんじゃなくて、くうらんのまえからなおす。……けしゴム、まだのこってますね。
n3.english: Yes, that's it. Don't erase a name; revise from before the blank. …We still have some eraser left.

n2.japanese: そう、それです。名前を消すんじゃなくて、空欄の前から書き直す。……消しゴム、まだずいぶん残ってますね。

n1.japanese: ええ、それです。名前を消すんじゃなくて、空欄の前から書き直す。……これなら、消しゴムもまだ残りますね。
n1.reading: ええ、それです。なまえをけすんじゃなくて、くうらんのまえからかきなおす。……これなら、けしゴムもまだのこりますね。
n1.english: Yes, that's it. Don't erase a name; rewrite from before the blank. …This way, we even have some eraser left.

nodes.description: Sophie strikes through the projected sentence, leaving every name on the board alone. Peter opens his notebook a finger's width, sees she has already begun the new line, and closes it again. 'Splendid,' he says, quietly enough that the projector fan nearly takes it.

scenes.goal: Write and perform a replacement introduction that keeps contributions traceable without inventing one maker, then turn the rehearsal toward the futures waiting after the final night.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: Will the new line still make sense from the back row when one early contribution remains unknown?
scenes.learnerNeed: A stance on how the spoken introduction names several kinds of contribution and preserves the part no source can assign.

nodes.description: A strip of paper covers the old sentence on the rehearsal script. Sophie writes a new opening above it while Peter moves to the back row. Beside the lectern, three source cards wait under the headings 道, 文章, and 写真; one early route still has no name.

nodes.intent: Offer a replacement stage line that follows routes, text, and photographs back as far as the sources allow, then stops honestly.
nodes.attentionTarget: the new spoken line and the three source cards beside it

n3.japanese: こうしよう。『このアトラスは、何人もの手を通ってきました。道、文、写真の出どころは、横のカードでたどれます。分からない線は、分からないまま残しています。』……後ろまで届くか、読んでみるね。

nodes.question: How should the stage introduction hold the atlas's many makers?

options.action: Let the source cards name who added each route, passage, or photograph, and leave the early route visibly unknown.

japaneseByBand.n3: 横のカードに、誰が何を足したか並べよう。最初の道だけは、名前を入れないで『分からない』のままにする。
japaneseByBand.n2: 横のカードに、誰がどの道や文章を足したか並べましょう。最初の道だけは、無理に名前を入れず『分からない』と残す。

options.action: Say plainly that no one person made it, then invite the audience to follow each visible contribution on the cards.

japaneseByBand.n3: 最初に『一人で作ったものではありません』と言ってから、横のカードを一枚ずつ見せよう。
japaneseByBand.n2: 最初に『一人で作ったものではありません』とはっきり言って、横のカードを一枚ずつたどってもらいましょう。
japaneseByBand.n1: 最初に『一人で作ったものではありません』と言い切ってから、横のカードを一枚ずつたどってもらおう。

nodes.resume: The learner has chosen how the introduction and source cards work together. Sophie reads the new line from the stage while Peter tests the one early route that still has no name.

nodes.intent: Test the revised introduction from the back row, ask about the unnamed first route, and notice that an honest stop works better than a quick false answer.
nodes.attentionTarget: the early-route card where Sophie's answer stops at 'we don't know'

n2.japanese: 後ろからでも分かりました。道はこの人、文章はこの人。最初の道だけは『分からない』で止まった。……もし一人の名前を入れてたら、そこだけ早く答えて、間違ってましたね。

n1.japanese: 後ろからでも追えました。道はこの人、文章はこの人。最初の道だけは『分からない』で止まった。……仮に一人の名前を入れていたら、そこだけ答えは早くて、間違ってましたね。

nodes.intent: Run the revised line once more and hear it clear the old blank without hiding the unknown route.
nodes.attentionTarget: the first-page introduction reaching the back row without stopping at a name

n3.japanese: じゃ、もう一回。『このアトラスは、何人もの手を通ってきました』。……今度は止まらなかった。分からない線も、そのまま残ってる。

nodes.intent: Turn the rehearsal page and point to the next genuinely open question: what each person will do after the final public night.
nodes.attentionTarget: the next cue card, headed 'after this night,' with Alex's line still blank

n2.japanese: 通じました。……次のカード、空いてますね。『この夜のあと、どこへ』。アレックスのところだけ、まだ何もない。これは明日、本人に聞きましょう。

nodes.description: Sophie clips the revised opening over the old one and runs it once without stopping. Peter turns the rehearsal page. The next card reads AFTER THIS NIGHT; Alex's name sits beneath it with no arrow, date, or destination. A cafe receipt is tucked under the corner for tomorrow.

callbacks.meaningNow: Peter's one question stops solving a problem and starts dissolving a false premise: instead of answering 'whose name owns the atlas,' he asks whether finishing it requires a single owner at all, and the class rejects the premise rather than picking a name.
callbacks.optionalFallback: A quiet classmate asks whether the first-page introduction needs one named maker at all, and the class rewrites the spoken line around the contributions it can actually trace.

outcomes.description: The class rejects the one-maker sentence, replaces it with a spoken introduction that traces routes, text, and photographs without inventing an owner, and tests the revision from the back row. The next rehearsal cue now asks where each person will go after the final night, with Alex's line still blank.

Peter returns from the edge of the room to reframe the class's deadlock with a single question; the ensemble, having learned at Chapter 34 that his quiet questioning is full participation, now waits for that question and builds the resolution around it instead of pressing him to perform or to supply a name himself.

Recognition of a counterfactual that challenges the false premise without flattening the speaker returns through the chapter's selected-response activity; the story emits no lesson-completion command.

replay.withdrawnContentFallback: Use the same premise-reframing with neutral nameplates and a generic quiet reviewer who asks whether the first-page introduction needs one maker, then tests a spoken line that keeps every traceable contribution and the unknown route visible.
